title: Creating Your AWS Account 🆕
description: Walk through the sign‑up process securely, and understand the root user vs IAM users.

slides.title: Before You Begin 📋
slides.content:
# What You’ll Need

To create an AWS account, gather:
- A valid **email address** (this will be your root login).
- A **credit or debit card** (AWS requires it even for Free Tier).
- A **phone number** for identity verification.
- A strong password.

> ⚠️ Use a personal email that you’ll have access to long‑term. Avoid shared addresses.

quizData.question: Why does AWS ask for a credit card during Free Tier sign‑up?

options.text: To charge you a small registration fee
To verify your identity and cover usage beyond Free Tier limits
It’s optional – you can skip it
To automatically upgrade your account after 30 days

quizData.explanation: The card is used for identity verification and to charge you if you exceed Free Tier limits. You can set up billing alarms to avoid that.

slides.title: Step 1: Go to the Sign‑Up Page 🔗
slides.content:
# Sign Up

Visit [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com) and click **Create an AWS Account**.

1. Enter your email and choose a **root account name** (e.g., your company name).
2. Verify your email with a code.
3. Set a **strong root password** (use a password manager!).

> **Root account**: This is the master key to your entire AWS kingdom. Guard it carefully.

slides.title: ⚠️ Root User Warning
slides.content:
## Never Use Root for Daily Tasks

The root user has unrestricted access to everything – billing, account deletion. Best practices:
- Create an **IAM user** for yourself immediately after sign‑up.
- Enable **multi‑factor authentication (MFA)** on the root account.
- Lock the root credentials away.

We’ll create IAM users in Chapter 3.

slides.title: Step 2: Contact & Billing Info 💳
slides.content:
# Enter Billing Details

Select **Personal** or **Professional** account type (both get Free Tier).

- Enter your address, phone number.
- Enter card details – a $1 authorisation charge may appear and vanish.
- Verify your phone via SMS or voice call.

After verification, you’ll be taken to the console automatically.

quizData.question: You should use your root account for everyday tasks like launching servers.

options.text: False – create IAM users for daily operations

quizData.explanation: The root account is for account and billing management only. For daily AWS tasks, create an IAM user with least privilege.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Multiple Accounts via AWS Organizations 🚀
slides.content:
## Separate Environments

As you grow, never put production and development in the same account. Use **AWS Organizations** to create multiple accounts linked under a single payer. This isolates resources and costs.

We’ll cover this in advanced chapters.
